official_measurement_examples.name: IRZ July 2026 update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's national SSSI Impact Risk Zones dataset was last updated 13 July 2026 and is maintained as a screening tool for planning consultation risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: Screening not decision
official_measurement_examples.fact: An IRZ hit indicates that the proposal type and scale may require further consideration or Natural England consultation; it is not an automatic planning refusal or approval.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consolidated threshold logic
official_measurement_examples.fact: IRZ output can consolidate overlapping site sensitivities and display the lowest relevant development threshold, so the displayed zone must not be read as a single-site parcel rule.

official_measurement_examples.name: SSSI units distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: SSSI units are management and condition subdivisions inside designated SSSIs and are distinct from the statutory SSSI boundary and the wider IRZ screening geography.

official_measurement_examples.name: Off-site effects
official_measurement_examples.fact: Activities outside an SSSI boundary can still require assessment or statutory advice where they are likely to damage the site's special interest.

official_measurement_examples.name: Landowner consent distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England consent for an operation on SSSI land is a separate statutory control from planning permission and must not be inferred from planning status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public body assent distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Public bodies use the SSSI assent/statutory-advice route for potentially damaging operations; assent is distinct from private landowner consent and planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: HRA separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where a SSSI also underpins a SAC, SPA or Ramsar site, Habitats Regulations assessment duties remain separate from the IRZ screening result.

core_rules: SSSI IRZ is a screening and consultation-support layer not a planning decision
an IRZ intersection is not automatic refusal
absence of an IRZ trigger is not proof no protected-site effect exists
SSSI statutory boundary is distinct from SSSI unit geometry
SSSI units are distinct from IRZ screening zones
overlapping IRZ thresholds must retain development type and scale context
Natural England consultation advice is not planning permission
SSSI consent is not planning permission
public-body assent is not private SSSI consent
off-site activities can affect SSSI special interest
European-site HRA duties remain separate from IRZ screening
protected-species licensing remains separate from protected-site controls
IRZ evidence does not determine land ownership
protected-site consultation does not reserve development capacity
no parcel SSSI clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
